name: Residences at Willow Park
headline: The Aurora Housing Authority is renovating its 68-unit project-based Section 8 townhome community, Residences at Willow Park at 14001 E. Colorado Drive, and adding a new building on the site, using a 2023-cycle federal 4% credit and $17 million of CHFA bonds for 86 income-restricted homes in total.
why_it_matters: A housing authority recapitalization that preserves 100% project-based Section 8 housing and adds new units on the same land; unit counts and bedroom mix differ across public sources and should be checked before relying on them.

status.label: Rehab and new building targeted for late 2025 to spring 2026; townhome waitlists reopened in 2026; completion not confirmed
status.detail: In October 2025 the housing authority told Aurora's housing policy committee that the new building would be complete by the end of 2025 and the renovation of the 68 existing units by spring 2026. The authority opened waitlists for the three-bedroom townhomes (January 2026) and two-bedroom townhomes (April 2026), and its leasing site welcomes 18 brand-new apartments at Willow Park Flats on the same site. No completion or 8609 record found; the deal is still on CHFA's 4% award report.

next_step: Watch Aurora Housing Authority and city committee updates for completion of the renovation and 8609 issuance.

key_numbers.meaning: CHFA lists 66 one- and 20 two-bedroom units: 4 at 30%, 26 at 50% and 56 at 60% AMI; the Section 8 column is marked Yes.

key_numbers.value: 68 existing units rehabbed plus a new building
key_numbers.meaning: The housing authority reported 22 new units in October 2025; its leasing site names 18 new apartments at Willow Park Flats.

facts.value: Family, new construction and acquisition/rehabilitation; in a QCT; not in a DDA or SADDA; Section 8 column marked Yes
68 units of project-based Section 8 (PBRA) and tax credit housing in 2- and 3-bedroom units, mostly multi-story townhomes, in 17 buildings; residents pay 30% of adjusted income
Complete interior rehab of all 68 existing units and a new three-story walk-up building with updated ADA-compliant apartments; designed to Enterprise Green Communities standards
18 brand-new affordable apartments on the same site, managed by the housing authority as a separate property and program

background.text: The housing authority described the project to Aurora's Housing, Neighborhood Services and Redevelopment Policy Committee on 2025-10-15 as an acquisition-rehabilitation of a 100% Section 8 property: a full interior rehab of 68 units plus a new 22-unit building, with the new building due by the end of 2025 and renovations finishing in spring 2026.

CHFA's count of 86 units equals the 68 existing units plus the 18 new Willow Park Flats apartments (inferred), even though the housing authority calls the Flats a separate property and program; the October 2025 update instead cited 22 new units.

In 2026 the housing authority reopened pre-application waitlists for the three-bedroom townhomes (on-site 2026-01-26 to 2026-01-28) and two-bedroom townhomes (on-site 2026-04-20 to 2026-04-22); the three-bedroom list has since closed.
The deal does not appear in CHFA's 2023 Round One or Round Two applicant reports or the 2023 Round Two award report.

timeline.event: Housing authority update to Aurora's housing policy committee: new building due end of 2025, rehab due spring 2026
Listed on CHFA's Federal 4% award report under cycle year 2023 (no 8609s issued yet)

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists 86 units, while the housing authority's October 2025 update describes 68 existing units plus 22 new units (90), and its leasing site describes 68 units at the Residences plus 18 new units at Willow Park Flats.
CHFA lists 66 one-bedroom and 20 two-bedroom units, while the housing authority and its engineer describe the Residences as two- and three-bedroom units.
